description: System-level A/B comparison of two host sets. Reads host metrics and eBPF only, so it is independent of which database engine, if any, is deployed.

links.title: Cassandra A/B Comparison
links.tooltip: The database side of the comparison, on a Cassandra cluster

panels.description: Change in the fraction of CPU time not spent idle. Idle over the sum of every state, so it is core-count independent and cannot leave 0 to 100. Negative is the candidate group doing the same work for less CPU.
panels.title: CPU busy

panels.description: Change in the one-minute load average of the group divided by its logical cores. Negative is a shorter run queue on the candidate.
panels.title: Load per core

panels.description: Change in bytes per second read plus written on the whole disks, per node. Positive is the candidate moving more data; check it against the workload's own throughput before calling it good.
panels.title: Disk throughput

panels.description: Change in the fraction of wall time the busiest disk had a request in flight. Negative is more device headroom on the candidate.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$candidate", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Disk busy

panels.description: Change in the 99th percentile block layer read service time, from the eBPF bio histogram. Negative is better.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Block I/O read p99

panels.description: Change in the 99th percentile block layer write service time, from the eBPF bio histogram. Negative is better.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Block I/O write p99

panels.description: Every host reporting host metrics, with the hardware it runs on. The Build column is filled in only where a Cassandra build label exists; on any other engine it is blank, which is expected.

targets.expr:
max by (host_name, cassandra_build) ((group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Hosts and hardware

panels.description: How many hosts are in each group right now. The groups do not have to be the same size; every aggregation on this page averages per host or forms a ratio, never a bare sum. A zero means that selection is empty and every delta above is meaningless.
panels.title: Hosts in each group

options.content:
This page compares what the **machine** is doing across two sets of hosts. It
reads host metrics and eBPF only, so it works whatever is running on the box:
a database of any kind, several at once, or nothing at all.

**Pick the groups first.** *Baseline* and *Candidate* are host sets, selected
from whichever hosts are reporting metrics. Put the hosts running the old
configuration in one and the new configuration in the other. Any split works:
one against two, two against two, one host against itself in a second cluster.

**The two sets should differ in exactly one thing.** A build, a JDK, a garbage
collector, a kernel setting, an instance type. If they differ in more than one,
nothing below tells you which one moved the number.

**Every aggregate is an average per host, or a ratio over the whole group.**
Never a bare sum, so groups of different sizes stay comparable. Ratios such as
CPU busy divide the group's total by the group's total, which weights by core
count and is what you want.

**Deltas** are `(candidate - baseline) / baseline` in percent. Green means the
candidate is better *for that metric*: lower for latency, CPU and queueing,
higher for throughput. A delta is blank when the baseline is zero.

**Ad-hoc filters** apply to every panel at once. Add `device`, `mountpoint`,
`state`, `direction` or `operation` filters to narrow the whole page without
editing a query. The *Group by* variable drives the last section, which ignores
the baseline and candidate selection and shows every host.

**Engine agnostic by default.** Every panel above the Slice and dice section
reads `system_*` from the hostmetrics receiver or `ebpf_exporter_*`. Those carry
`host_name` and `cluster` and no engine label, so nothing here depends on which
database is deployed.

**Two exceptions, both labelled:**

- The *JVM allocation rate* pair reads `jvm_memory_allocation_bytes_sum`. It
  fills in for a JVM engine and is empty for anything else. Empty is the correct
  reading there, not a fault.
- *Group by* offers `cassandra_build` as an optional dimension. It is joined in
  through a map that falls back to a plain host entry, so on a non-Cassandra
  cluster those panels collapse to one unlabelled series rather than going
  blank.

**Not collected on this cluster — no panel is built on these:**

- `system_filesystem_utilization` — optional hostmetrics metric, not enabled.
  The *Filesystem used* panel computes the same ratio from
  `system_filesystem_usage_bytes` instead.
- `system_paging_usage_bytes` and `system_paging_utilization` — these hosts have
  no swap device, so the scraper emits nothing.

**Two upstream scaling bugs are corrected in the queries.** The hostmetrics
paging scraper multiplies both counters by the 4096 byte page size:

- `system_paging_operations_total` stores kilobytes times 4096. The panel
  divides by 4 to get bytes per second.
- `system_paging_faults_total` stores the fault count times 4096. The panel
  divides by 4096 to get faults per second.

Both factors were confirmed against `/proc/vmstat` on a live host.

**Disk panels select whole disks only** (`nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+`). Partitions repeat
the whole-disk counters in `/proc/diskstats`, and the data device does not carry
the same name on every host.

**Network panels exclude virtual interfaces** (loopback, veth, CNI, flannel,
tailscale) so overlay traffic is not counted twice.

panels.description: Fraction of CPU time not idle, as idle over the sum of every state across the group. Core-count independent, so it cannot go negative or exceed 100.
panels.title: CPU busy

panels.description: Non-idle CPU time as a percent of the group's logical cores, split by scheduler state. The states sum to the CPU busy figure beside it. A group that moves time from user to system, or into softirq, is doing different work for the same throughput.
panels.title: CPU time by state

panels.description: One-minute load average summed over the group, divided by its logical cores. Above 1.0 means more runnable work than cores. Normalising by core count keeps mixed instance sizes comparable.
panels.title: Load average per core

panels.description: Time the CPU was blocked on the hypervisor (steal) or on I/O (wait), as a percent of the group's cores. Steal above zero means the comparison is being distorted by a noisy neighbour, not by the change under test.
panels.title: Stolen and I/O wait time

panels.description: Every memory state stacked, averaged over the baseline hosts. Compare the shape against the candidate panel beside it: a host holding less page cache for the same working set will read more from disk.
panels.title: Memory composition, baseline

panels.description: Every memory state stacked, averaged over the candidate hosts. Same axis as the baseline panel beside it.
panels.title: Memory composition, candidate

panels.description: The `used` state: memory that is neither cache, buffers nor free. Whatever the processes on the host actually hold.
panels.title: Anonymous memory in use

panels.description: Cached plus buffered memory. This is the read cache in front of the data disk; a smaller cache under the same load pushes reads down to the block layer.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_memory_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$candidate", state=~"cached|buffered"})))
  - (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_memory_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$baseline", state=~"cached|buffered"})))
) / (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_memory_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$baseline", state=~"cached|buffered"})))

panels.title: Page cache resident

panels.description: eBPF `cache_writes` per second: writes that landed in page cache. Tracks the write path above the block layer.
panels.title: Page cache write rate

panels.description: eBPF `page_mark_dirties` per second: pages newly marked dirty, which is future writeback work. A rising dirty rate with flat disk throughput means writeback is falling behind.
panels.title: Dirty page rate

panels.description: JVM ONLY. Bytes allocated per second, summed over every arena and averaged per host. Allocation pressure sets GC frequency, so it belongs beside the CPU panels. On a non-JVM engine this panel is empty, which is the correct reading rather than a fault.
panels.title: JVM allocation rate

panels.description: JVM ONLY. The same allocation rate split by arena. TLAB is the fast thread-local path; Main is the slow path taken by objects too large for a TLAB. A shift from TLAB to Main means bigger objects. Empty on a non-JVM engine.
panels.title: JVM allocation rate by arena

panels.description: Bytes per second on the whole disks, split by direction and averaged per host. Partitions are excluded because they repeat the whole-disk counters.
panels.title: Disk throughput

panels.description: Completed I/O operations per second by direction, averaged per host. Read next to throughput: the same bytes at more operations means a smaller average request.
panels.title: Disk IOPS

panels.description: 99th percentile block layer read service time from the eBPF bio histogram. This is the device and its queue, below the filesystem and below page cache. Lower is better.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Block I/O read latency p99

panels.description: 99th percentile block layer write service time from the eBPF bio histogram. Lower is better.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Block I/O write latency p99

panels.description: 99th percentile XFS read operation latency. Above the block layer, so it includes page cache hits; the gap against block I/O read p99 is what the cache is absorbing. Empty on a host with no XFS filesystem.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="read"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: XFS read latency p99

panels.description: 99th percentile XFS write operation latency. Buffered writes return on the cache write, so this normally sits far below block I/O write p99.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$candidate", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket{host_name=~"$baseline", operation="write"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: XFS write latency p99

panels.description: Percent of wall time the busiest disk on a host had at least one request in flight. The saturation signal: near 100 the device, not the change under test, is setting the pace.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$candidate", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (100 * avg(max by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Disk busy

panels.description: Requests in flight on the whole disks, averaged per host. Rising queue with flat throughput is the classic saturation shape.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_disk_pending_operations{host_name=~"$candidate", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"})))
  - (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_disk_pending_operations{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"})))
) / (avg(sum by (host_name) (system_disk_pending_operations{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"})))

panels.title: Disk queue depth

panels.description: Total operation time divided by operations completed, in milliseconds. The mean companion to the block I/O percentiles; a mean that stays flat while p99 climbs means a tail, not a shift.

targets.expr:
100 * (
    (1000 * avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operation_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$candidate", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))
         / sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operations_total{host_name=~"$candidate", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
  - (1000 * avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operation_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))
         / sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operations_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))
) / (1000 * avg(sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operation_time_seconds_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))
         / sum by (host_name) (rate(system_disk_operations_total{host_name=~"$baseline", device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]))))

panels.title: Average I/O service time

panels.description: Requests per second the kernel merged with an adjacent request before issuing them. High merge counts mean sequential access that the elevator could coalesce.
panels.title: Merged I/O rate

panels.description: Used bytes over total bytes per mount point, averaged across the hosts of each group. The data mount is the one to watch; root and boot are shown so a full root is not missed.

targets.expr:
100 * avg by (mountpoint) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$baseline", state="used"})
      / avg by (mountpoint) (sum by (host_name, mountpoint) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$baseline"}))

100 * avg by (mountpoint) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$candidate", state="used"})
      / avg by (mountpoint) (sum by (host_name, mountpoint) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes{host_name=~"$candidate"}))

panels.title: Filesystem used

panels.description: Free bytes per mount point, averaged across the hosts of each group. Absolute headroom, which matters more than a percentage on a large data volume.
panels.title: Filesystem free

panels.description: Bytes per second paged in and out, from `/proc/vmstat` pgpgin and pgpgout. With no swap device this is page cache traffic, so it should track disk throughput. The query divides the stored value by 4 to correct an upstream scaling bug; see the caveats panel.
panels.title: Paging throughput

panels.description: Major and minor page faults per second. Major faults need a disk read and are the expensive ones. The query divides the stored value by 4096 to correct an upstream scaling bug; see the caveats panel.
panels.title: Page fault rate

panels.description: Bytes per second on the physical interfaces by direction, averaged per host. Virtual interfaces are excluded so overlay traffic is not counted twice.
panels.title: Network throughput

panels.description: Packets per second by direction, averaged per host. Bytes divided by packets is the average frame size, which shifts when a workload changes its message batching.
panels.title: Network packet rate

panels.description: Interface errors per second. Anything above zero invalidates a latency comparison; find the cause before reading any other panel.
panels.title: Network errors

panels.description: Packets dropped per second at the interface. Usually a full receive ring, which surfaces as retries and tail latency in the client.
panels.title: Network drops

panels.description: Process and thread counts by scheduler status, averaged per host. `blocked` is the one to watch: tasks in uninterruptible sleep are waiting on I/O and never appear in the load-average story.
panels.title: Processes by status

panels.description: Processes forked per second. Steady background noise from the agents; a step change means something started spawning work.
panels.title: Process creation rate

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and cassandra_build only. This is a ratio of idle time to total time, so grouping it by state is degenerate and returns idle at zero; use the CPU time by state panel above for the state breakdown. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
100 * (1 - sum by ($groupby) (rate(system_cpu_time_seconds_total{state="idle"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))
         / sum by ($groupby) (rate(system_cpu_time_seconds_total[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)))))

panels.title: CPU busy by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and state. With state selected this becomes the full memory composition across the cluster. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
sum by ($groupby) (system_memory_usage_bytes * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Memory in use by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and device and direction. Whole disks only. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
sum by ($groupby) (rate(system_disk_io_bytes_total{device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Disk throughput by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and device. Percent of wall time with a request in flight; the maximum within a group, because a saturated disk must not be diluted by an idle one. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
100 * max by ($groupby) (rate(system_disk_io_time_seconds_total{device=~"nvme[0-9]+n[0-9]+"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Disk busy by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and device and operation. Set Group by to device to find which disk carries the tail. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, $groupby) (rate(ebpf_exporter_bio_latency_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)))))

panels.title: Block I/O latency p99 by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and operation. Set Group by to operation to separate read, write, open and sync; sync dominates the tail whenever a journal flush is in flight. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, $groupby) (rate(ebpf_exporter_xfs_latency_seconds_bucket[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)))))

panels.title: XFS latency p99 by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and device and direction. Virtual interfaces are excluded. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
sum by ($groupby) (rate(system_network_io_bytes_total{device!~"lo|veth.*|cni.*|flannel.*|tailscale.*|docker.*|br-.*"}[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Network throughput by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and operation. `cache_writes` are writes into page cache; `page_mark_dirties` are pages queued for writeback. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
sum by ($groupby) (rate(ebpf_exporter_page_cache_ops_total[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Page cache operations by ${groupby}

panels.description: Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and device and mountpoint. Used bytes over total bytes for the selected dimension. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
100 * sum by ($groupby) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes{state="used"} * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))
      / sum by ($groupby) (system_filesystem_usage_bytes * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
       unless on(host_name) group by (host_name) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes))))

panels.title: Filesystem used by ${groupby}

panels.description: JVM ONLY. Grouped by ${groupby} across every host, ignoring the baseline and candidate selection. Honours host_name, cluster and arena. Empty on a non-JVM engine, which is the correct reading rather than a fault. cassandra_build is optional and joined in: on a cluster without that label the panel collapses to one unlabelled series rather than going blank.

targets.expr:
sum by ($groupby) (rate(jvm_memory_allocation_bytes_sum[$__rate_interval]) * on(host_name) group_left(cassandra_build) (group by (host_name, cassandra_build) (cassandra_storage_load_bytes)
   or (group by (host_name) (system_cpu_logical_count)
